questions.q: What does the derivative f'(a) formally represent?
options: The average rate of change of f over the whole domain
The value of f at the point a
The limit of the average rate of change as the interval shrinks to zero, i.e. the instantaneous rate of change
The area under f between 0 and a
questions.explain: f'(a) = lim_{h->0} [f(a+h) - f(a)] / h, which is the slope of the tangent line at a, not an average over an interval.

questions.q: If f(S) = ln(S), what is f'(S)?
questions.explain: The derivative of the natural log is 1/S by the standard rule d/dx ln(x) = 1/x.

questions.q: Which differentiation rule is used to differentiate a composition like f(g(x))?
questions.explain: The chain rule states d/dx f(g(x)) = f'(g(x)) * g'(x), exactly the tool for compositions.

questions.q: In finance, an option's delta is best described as which calculus object?
options: The second derivative of the option value with respect to time
The derivative of the option value with respect to the underlying price, dV/dS
The integral of the option payoff over all prices
The average option price over the last year
questions.explain: Delta measures how much an option's value moves per one-dollar move in the underlying, which is precisely dV/dS.

questions.q: Why is the central finite difference (f(a+h)-f(a-h))/(2h) generally preferred over the one-sided version (f(a+h)-f(a))/h for numerical derivatives?
options: Its approximation error shrinks faster (like h^2 instead of h) as h gets small
questions.explain: The central difference cancels the first-order error term, so its error is O(h^2), making it more accurate than the one-sided O(h) estimate for the same step size.
